verdict.rationale: MotherDuck's MCP docs point to a dedicated 'Restricting to read-only access' option for limiting an AI assistant's privileges, and data can be shared with specific roles or accounts to scope read access, so the product offers some first-party least-privilege controls for agents (motherduck-docs-31, motherduck-docs-10, motherduck-docs-47). The evidence never shows how API tokens or credentials are issued, nor any per-token scopes, expiry or agent-specific credential types. missing for 10: documented issuance of scoped/least-privilege API tokens, per-credential scope granularity beyond read-only vs read-write, token lifecycle (expiry/revocation), independent or hands-on corroboration
